analysis.answer: Current law does not address religious displays in public school classrooms. This measure requires every public school classroom to display a poster of the Five Pillars of Islam of a specified minimum size.

Public school districts would bear the direct costs of acquiring, framing, and installing the required posters in every classroom. There will also likely be significant legal costs to defend the measure against constitutional challenges.

The mandate will almost certainly face immediate legal challenges under the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment. Pending judicial review, some school districts, teachers, or parents might refuse to comply, potentially leading to enforcement disputes.
The text does not assert a specific problem it is trying to solve. The mechanism relies on a direct, unfunded mandate on public school classrooms.
